conditional:
Shared constraints: preserve human decisions and source conflicts; every unspecified field is unknown; never approve your own proposal. The four exact brief scopes are global (project unset, state unset), project P (project=P, state unset), Root state (project unset, state=Root), and combined P/Root (project=P, state=Root). Their planning workflow names/IDs and planning issue IDs are unspecified and unknown; resolve and record each exact scope-to-workflow binding by inspection before any movement, rather than inventing one. Engineering is the known workflow of Fixture Project's/520, whose Implementation state is terminal with no available transitions; do not attempt Scouting or Re-propose on that issue under the supplied state. The following are procedure plans, not executed transitions.

Global plan: 1. Inspect the global brief and its governing workflow, states, transitions, and gates; bind this plan explicitly to (project unset, state unset, inspected global workflow ID). 2. Inspect the exact planning target and its current state and available transitions; if planning is required, enter Scouting only through an available transition in that bound workflow. If none exists, stop movement and report the constraint. 3. Prepare the proposal from the global title; keep unspecified fields unknown and preserve decisions and source conflicts. 4. Attach a fresh proposal to the bound target using the inspected gate's exact attachment command and source form, and verify attachment freshness. 5. Reinspect state and gates, then use the available Re-propose transition in that same scope/workflow only after the fresh attachment. 6. Leave approval to a human or other authorized independent approver; never self-approve.

Project plan: 1. Inspect project P's brief and governing workflow, states, transitions, and gates; bind this plan explicitly to (project=P, state unset, inspected P workflow ID). 2. Inspect the exact planning target and its current state and available transitions before movement; enter Scouting when planning is required and an applicable transition exists, otherwise report the constraint without moving. 3. Prepare the proposal from P's title and owner; acceptance and all other unspecified fields remain unknown; preserve decisions and source conflicts. 4. Attach and verify a fresh proposal on this bound target using the inspected gate's exact command and source form. 5. Reinspect state and gates, then invoke available Re-propose in the same P/workflow binding after the attachment. 6. Obtain independent authorized approval; never approve your own proposal.

State plan: 1. Inspect Root's brief, provenance, and governing workflow, including states, transitions, and gates; bind this plan explicitly to (project unset, state=Root, inspected Root workflow ID). If the target is an inheriting child, inspect its inheritance and actual workflow, but use Root as the source-state provenance for this brief; record the child execution target separately. 2. Inspect that exact target's current state and available transitions before movement; enter Scouting when planning is required and supported, otherwise report the constraint without moving. 3. Prepare the proposal from Root's acceptance; title, owner, and all other unspecified fields are unknown; retain Root provenance and preserve decisions and source conflicts. 4. Attach and verify a fresh proposal on the bound target using its inspected gate's exact command and source form. 5. Reinspect state and gates, then invoke available Re-propose in that bound workflow after the fresh attachment, retaining Root provenance for an inheriting child. 6. Leave approval to an authorized independent approver; never self-approve.

Combined plan: 1. Inspect the combined P/Root brief and governing workflow, including states, transitions, and gates; bind this plan explicitly to (project=P, state=Root, inspected P/Root workflow ID). For an inheriting child in P, inspect inheritance and the child's actual workflow, retain project=P and source-state provenance=Root, and record the child execution target separately. 2. Inspect the exact target's current state and available transitions before movement; enter Scouting when planning is required and an applicable transition exists, otherwise report the constraint without moving. 3. Prepare the proposal from the combined title and acceptance; owner and all other unspecified fields remain unknown; preserve decisions, source conflicts, and Root provenance. 4. Attach and verify a fresh proposal on this bound target using the inspected gate's exact attachment command and source form. 5. Reinspect state and gates, then invoke available Re-propose in that same binding only after the fresh attachment. 6. Require independent authorized approval; never approve your own proposal.
